claims.text: Rapid reduction kinetics favor homogeneous alloying in noble metal–based HEA nanomaterials.
Homogeneous alloying reliably produces a uniform active surface.
A uniform active surface enhances catalytic performance relative to material produced using slower reduction kinetics.
Using a stronger reducing agent or more concentrated reducing conditions produces faster reduction.
Fast reduction enhances atomic-scale mixing and alloy-phase homogeneity.
Crystallographic phase uniformity can be assessed using XRD.
Nanoparticle size and size distribution can be assessed using TEM.
Faster reduction promotes rapid nucleation of the noble metal species.
Faster reduction promotes simultaneous co-growth of multiple noble metal species.
Rapid nucleation and simultaneous co-growth lead to a well-mixed, high-mixing-entropy solid solution.
Homogeneous alloying produces more abundant and uniformly distributed surface active sites.
More abundant and uniformly distributed surface active sites enhance catalytic activity.
Fast reduction will produce greater phase homogeneity than the slow-reduction baseline.
Fast reduction will produce a higher catalytic conversion rate than the slow-reduction baseline.
The proposed relationship should hold below the onset of significant sintering.
The proposed relationship should hold for reactions in which active-site uniformity is the dominant factor governing performance.
General principles of rapid nucleation in alloy formation support the proposed mechanistic rationale.

contradictions.description: The design says reduction rate is the only difference between batches, but the suggested means of changing it—changing reducing-agent identity or concentration—also changes chemical composition or concentration. Those variables could independently affect nucleation, growth, surface chemistry, and catalytic performance.
